bug_semantics: An adjacent-network attacker could send a crafted mDNS response whose TXT, HINFO, A, or AAAA payload length exceeded the bytes actually available or whose decoded payload did not consume exactly the record's declared RDLENGTH. Python byte slicing silently returned a short payload while DNSIncoming advanced its offset by the attacker-declared length; _read_others appended the resulting record before a later parse error, answers() returned the already-appended prefix, and RecordManager then inserted those records into DNSCache for ServiceInfo consumers.
flaw_origin: Commit e814dd1e6848d8c7ec03660d347ea4a34390c37d replaced readString's exact-width struct.unpack with the raw slice self.data[self.offset:self.offset+length] while still advancing by length. That change first made truncated reads non-failing. The code subsequently moved and was renamed; ac081cf00addde1ceea2c076f73905fdb293de3a later inlined the same already-vulnerable slice behavior into _read_character_string rather than introducing it.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names William McBrine <wmcbrine@gmail.com> as both author and committer and its message contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker
evidence: The published CVE.org record at https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-48487 states that versions before 0.149.16 are affected, describes attacker-declared RDLENGTH advancing _read_character_string/_read_string past _data_len and contaminating DNSCache/ServiceInfo, and identifies 544449596e645fcaad3834fa0cb614a54f847a82 and release 0.149.16 as the fix.

git diff 488de8826ddd58646358900d057a4a1632492948 e814dd1e6848d8c7ec03660d347ea4a34390c37d -- Zeroconf.py shows readString changed from struct.unpack of an exact calculated width to info = self.data[self.offset:self.offset+length], followed by self.offset += length.

Direct parent-tree verification with git show 488de8826ddd58646358900d057a4a1632492948:Zeroconf.py shows lines 511-517 using struct.unpack(format, self.data[self.offset:self.offset+length]); a short slice cannot satisfy the declared struct width and therefore raises before returning or appending a truncated record.

git log -L across Zeroconf.py, zeroconf/__init__.py, zeroconf/dns.py, zeroconf/_dns.py, zeroconf/_protocol.py, and src/zeroconf/_protocol/incoming.py traces the vulnerable slice back through moves, formatting, typing, and renames to e814dd1e6848d8c7ec03660d347ea4a34390c37d; tag --contains plus version sorting shows 0.13 as its earliest release tag.

git show ac081cf00addde1ceea2c076f73905fdb293de3a -- src/zeroconf/_protocol/incoming.py shows _read_character_string changed from calling the already-vulnerable _read_string(length) to an equivalent direct slice and offset increment, so this later optimization preserved rather than introduced the flaw.

At fix parent 28bb01f23951f7883d8c3af66b6d537c34c516c7, src/zeroconf/_protocol/incoming.py lines 253-265 slice without checking _data_len, lines 283-301 append rec without requiring self.offset == end, and answers() lines 188-200 catches a later decode exception and returns the accumulated _answers.

At the same vulnerable tree, src/zeroconf/_handlers/record_manager.py lines 77-91 obtains msg.answers(), lines 117-125 accepts unexpired records, and lines 154-158 calls cache.async_add_records; src/zeroconf/_services/info.py lines 430-441 parses cached TXT bytes into properties.

git show 544449596e645fcaad3834fa0cb614a54f847a82 adds _data_len overrun checks to both payload readers and drops/resynchronizes any record for which self.offset != the declared end; its regression tests cover truncated TXT, HINFO, A, and cross-record RDLENGTH mismatch.

reasoning: The advisory is a real published CVE/GHSA, and local source confirms its parser-to-cache path. The atomic causal change is e814dd1e6848d8c7ec03660d347ea4a34390c37d: before it, exact-width struct.unpack rejected an undersized payload; after it, slicing silently accepted the bytes present and advanced by the declared length. History following identified moves and later optimizations does not reveal a smaller later introducer; notably ac081cf00addde1ceea2c076f73905fdb293de3a merely duplicated the existing slice semantics for character strings. The direct parent proves absence, and the 0.13 tag establishes that the BIC precedes affected releases. Fix 544449596e645fcaad3834fa0cb614a54f847a82 reverses the unsafe behavior with explicit bounds and exact-RDLENGTH consumption checks, is patch-equivalent to both PR member commits, and is included in the first successfully published patched package 0.149.16. Because the BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no AI marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI regardless of unrelated AI-signaled commits elsewhere in the repository.
